messages:
maria: quick question — integrating the JS SDK with our service account flows and hitting a weird edge. Do you recommend minting a JWT and exchanging for an access token server->server, or doing OIDC token exchange for the SDK flow? also, how should clients express org vs project scoping — should scope live in the JWT claims, or do we pass org/project in the API request?

alex: short answer: server-to-server = JWT -> exchange. OIDC is for browser/federated users. JWTs are fine for backend SDKs. put authorization granularity in the access token (scopes/claims) or in the request headers — not the raw JWT metadata.

alex: example (very rough):
```bash
# create signed JWT (iss=svc-account, aud=token-exchange)
cat <<EOF >payload.json
{
  "iss": "svc-account@example.iam",
  "sub": "svc-account@example.iam",
  "aud": "https://auth.example.com/token",
  "exp": 1710000000,
  "iat": 1709996400
}
EOF
# sign with KMS or local key and POST to token endpoint to get access_token
curl -X POST https://auth.example.com/token -d @signed-jwt
```

samir: adding on — for org/project: prefer putting an explicit claim like `resource` or `scope` in the token that's understood by our authz layer. e.g. `resource:org:acme` or `resource:project:acme/proj-1`. That way token binds to the intended resource rather than relying on request params which are easier to spoof.

samir: if you're using impersonation (service account A impersonates B), use the token-exchange/impersonate endpoint and include `delegates` + the target scope. SDKs should call impersonation endpoint and store the short-lived access_token.

maria: thanks — is there any nuance with the SDK's retry/streaming paths? i.e., if token renewal happens mid-stream will the SDK re-auth and keep the stream, or do we expect a reconnect?

tia: good catch. right now our streaming client does not transparently refresh mid-stream. if the token TTL < expected stream duration you'll get a 401 and the client will close. two options: 1) mint tokens long enough for stream lifetime; 2) update SDK to support token refresh handshake (fetch new token and resume).

kevin: i'm prepping a small PR to add a token-refresh hook to the streaming transport. plan: expose an async `getAccessToken()` callback in the client config so callers can supply dynamic tokens (supports KMS-backed signing, impersonation, or a local refresh loop). will add tests for reconnect vs resume behavior. pinging @alex for API shape review.

alex: sounds good. `getAccessToken()` is the right abstraction. SDK shouldn't own how tokens are minted. keep it simple: SDK calls the callback before starting stream and on 401 to attempt a single refresh+retry. for long-lived sessions we can add background refresh later.

maria: example SDK usage I'd like to see:
```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  getAccessToken: async () => {
    // exchange jwt or call impersonate endpoint
    return await fetchTokenForServiceAccount();
  },
  resourceHint: 'org:acme', // optional metadata we pass to server for logging/authn
});

// streaming call
const stream = client.streamPredict({ model: 'r-infer-v1', prompt });
stream.on('data', chunk => console.log(chunk));
```

samir: also document the claim names we read server-side. current authz expects `resource` and `scp` (scopes). we'll add a small compatibility note: if `org`/`project` are present as top-level claims we map them into `resource`.

kevin: PR will include examples for JS + Python, and a short note about TTL vs streaming. will drop a draft link later today.

maria: thanks everyone. last check — are there any KMS/hsm requirements if we sign JWTs server-side?

infra-bot: for prod service accounts we require KMS signing (HSM-backed) for private keys. dev tokens can use local keys but flagged by infra. see infra/security#142 for policy.

devex-bot: created issue devex/sdk#789 to track: "SDK: getAccessToken hook + streaming token-refresh docs" — assigned to @kevin. :spiral_note_pad: please add code samples and a short migration note.

maria: perfect. i'll wait for the PR and update the integration. cheers :raised_hands:
